brief.topic: AI PMs who can't explain a trade-off to engineers
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Describe model and prompt trade-offs with eval results, cost and latency instead of adjectives, because engineers can check a number.

hooks.notes: Short and true; the reel shows the replacement.

hooks.text: Stop saying the new model ‘feels smarter’.
How to win a model debate with engineers.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): readable at a glance, and the reel flips each vague claim into a checkable one.

scenes.purpose: State the idea so it is clear from frame 0.
scenes.onScreen: Engineers don’t trust adjectives. / Bring numbers they can check.

storyboard.visual: Display headline with highlighted phrase; slate sub-line.
storyboard.animation: Readable on frame 0; underline sweep at 6; sub rises at 18.

scenes.purpose: Show how PMs describe trade-offs today.
scenes.onScreen: WHAT PMS SAY / Adjectives, not evidence. / VAGUE “It feels smarter” · VAGUE “Quality is way better” · VAGUE “It’s worth the cost”
scenes.voiceover: What PMs say: it feels smarter. Quality is way better. It’s worth the cost.

scenes.purpose: Replace each adjective with a checkable number (illustrative).
scenes.onScreen: WHAT TO SAY · ILLUSTRATIVE / Numbers they can check. / EVAL +6 passes on our 50-case set · EVAL Wins 31 of 50 blind pairs · PRICE 2x cost per task, +0.8s wait
scenes.voiceover: What to say instead, illustrative numbers: six more passes on our fifty-case set. Wins thirty-one of fifty blind comparisons. And the price: twice the cost per task and almost a second more wait.

storyboard.visual: Same card stack (hard cut), new headline; each card flips to its counterpart.

scenes.onScreen: Name the gain and the price in numbers. / Share this with a PM pitching models
scenes.voiceover: Name the gain and the price, in numbers. Share this with a PM pitching models.

storyboard.visual: Takeaway lines, last highlighted; CTA pill; end card.
storyboard.animation: Lines rise; CTA at 40; end card at 70.

scenes.cta: Share this with a PM pitching models

caption.opening: “It feels smarter” starts an argument. “+6 passes on our eval set, at 2x the cost” starts a decision.
body:
Swap adjectives for evidence engineers can check:
→ eval pass rate on a fixed set
→ blind side-by-side wins
→ cost per task and added latency
Always say both sides: the gain and the price. (The numbers in the reel are illustrative.)
caption.cta: Share this with a PM pitching models.

primaryCta.text: Share this with a PM pitching models

claims.text: PMs communicate AI trade-offs more effectively with eval results, cost and latency than with qualitative descriptions.
+6 passes on a 50-case set; 31 of 50 blind wins; 2x cost per task; +0.8s latency.
